evidence_detail: Counts reproduce exactly (257 modelling rows, 221 common set, baseline 5.0932; neutral filter 279 KEEP / 27 EXCLUDE; the 10 sulfone_sulfoxide members are all correctly excluded ionic liquids). BUT 110/257 'phase-verified liquid' rows rest on a FABRICATED melting point: fetch_pubchem_mp_b100.py:147-163 falls back to 'the first bare number in any free-text string', and PUG-View/HSDB entries begin with the compound name, so mp_C becomes 1.0 (85 molecules), 2.0 (18), 3.0 (6), -1.0 (1) degC, labelled ASSUMED_C. audit_b100_phase_state.py:121-126 prefers that value and :157 sets phase_verified=true because 1-3 degC < T; mp_note is not carried into phase_state_audit_b100.csv, so the caveat disappears before admission. 100 of the 221 evaluation molecules are in this set. Dropping them leaves 147 phase-verified (gate >=100 still met, but the margin is 47, not 157) and the freeze-manifest hard gate 'achieved_qualified=257' is inflated. Independent defect: build_b100_molecule_registry.py:61 nitro SMARTS [NX3](=O)=O cannot match RDKit's charge-separated nitro (verified: nitrobenzene, nitromethane, nitroglycerin all fail), so family 'nitro'=0 while 16 nitro/nitrate molecules are labelled 'amine' (1-Nitropropane, Nitrobenzene, Ethyl nitrate, Nitroglycerin ...) and the 'families meeting target' count is partly an artefact.

All six blocks reproduce to 4 dp with an independent numpy ridge under the same protocol: X0 4.3992, X1 4.3265, Xn 4.1030, X0+X1 3.6885, X0+X1+Xn 3.2999, dipole_only 4.3470; R2, RMSE, bias, lambda_median and cv_mae_for_pvalue match too (X0 lam_med=10.0 cv=4.3557; Xn 100.0/4.1241; X0X1Xn 100.0/3.3513). n_common=221 and constant baseline 5.0932 confirmed. No leakage: standardisation means/sds and lambda are fitted on the training fold only (run_b100_experiments.py:147-153, :168-194) - if the scaler had seen the held-out row my reproduction would not match. Defects: (a) p_label_permutation and p_feature_permutation are written as 0.0 for all six blocks (:364-374) from 200 permutations (:357) with no +1 correction, so the smallest reportable value is 1/201=0.005 and '0.0' is impossible; (b) N_PERM=1000 (:56) is declared and never used, and the executed count is not recorded in the manifest; (c) e1['note'] (:428) and the docstring (:11-13) say inner leave-one-out while choose_lambda actually runs inner 5-fold (:168-194); (d) X0 is 18 columns in build_b100_model_matrix.py:250 but 15 in run_b100_experiments.py:48. My own 2000-permutation nulls put the observed cv_mae below every draw (min null MAE 5.0044 label / 5.0262 feature for X0 vs observed 4.3557), i.e. p<0.0005: the conclusion survives, the printed '0.0' does not. The two nulls are the same exchangeability test seen twice, not independent corroboration (both give identical p). Sample note: the 36 dropped molecules are systematically higher-epsilon (mean 16.68 vs 7.61, max 178.5 vs 114.9) because they lack polarizability_au; X0 re-run on the full 257 gives MAE 5.6502 vs baseline 6.9083 (-18.2%), so the qualitative claim is robust to the restriction. PASS is conditional on dataset_257.

No leakage: the whole family is removed from training (run_b100_experiments.py:457-465) and lambda is chosen on the training fold only (:464); halocarbon also reproduces its r2=-18.5. Defects: (a) 12 families exist but 4 are silently dropped by the size filters (:455-461), so '6/8' is a subset of the taxonomy and the 4 are never named; (b) the 'amine' family (n_test 17) is 16 nitro/nitrate compounds mislabelled by build_b100_molecule_registry.py:61, so the reported amine row is not an amine result and E4's per-family text cannot be used as chemistry; (c) counting families is not a test: 6/8 successes under p=0.5 gives P(X>=6)=0.1445 (two-sided 0.289), so '6/8 families beat baseline' is not distinguishable from chance and needs per-family CIs; (d) r2 is taken about the test mean while beats_baseline uses the train mean, so rows read inconsistently (ester r2=+0.14 but beats_baseline=false; halocarbon r2=-18.5).

Verified exactly. oracle 39.0900, model top-10 mean 20.9661, pool 7.6095, regret 18.1239 all reproduce; my nested-LOO predictions agree with e6_ranking_b100.csv to 4.9e-5 (CSV rounding), which proves the Top-k IS chosen on the out-of-fold LOO predictions (run_b100_experiments.py:500-552) and not on in-sample fits - no leakage, and the null correctly resamples 10-subsets from the same 221-molecule pool. Exact enumeration over all C(221,10)=6.2292e16 subsets by integer knapsack gives P(mean>=20.9661)=0.003552 (221261548929500/62292206224983306); independent 200k Monte-Carlo with a different generator gives 0.003680 +/- 0.000135; the manifest's 0.003575 is 0.17 sigma from exact, so the reported p is right. Defects (reporting only): the method string says n=257 (:573) although n_pool=221; the k=15 sensitivity p is written as 0.0 from 20000 draws (:583-591) when its floor is 5e-5; the MC seed is not recorded in the manifest. Substantive caveat that must travel with the verdict: the model captures (20.9661-7.6095)/(39.09-7.6095)=42% of the achievable lift, and regret 18.12 is 2.4x the pool mean.

The group table reproduces exactly: WEAK n=159 MAE 2.5022 base 1.8199 median eps 4.39; INTERMEDIATE 47 / 3.0157 / 4.6647; STRONG n=15 / 18.3716 / 12.1596 / 27.4. But supports_h4=true is not supportable. (1) The comparison metric MAE/median_epsilon (run_b100_experiments.py:644-655) is not a skill metric: by skill = 1 - MAE/baseline BOTH groups are worse than a constant, WEAK -0.375 and STRONG -0.511, i.e. the model has no positive skill in the very group the hypothesis says it predicts best, so 'systematically better in low-eps weak association' is contradicted by the group's own constant baseline. (2) The strata are defined by thresholds on the target (eps<10 protic-free / eps>=20, build_b100_model_matrix.py:238-243), which truncates within-group variance by construction and mechanically shrinks relative error in the low band - the comparison is conditioned on the outcome. (3) n_strong=15<20, power.sufficient=false (:659-664), yet the comparison block is still emitted and the final report prints 'supports_h4=true' beside INSUFFICIENT_POWER. (4) The 15 STRONG molecules are themselves an artefact of the polarizability-driven common-set restriction (25 molecules with eps>=20 in 257 vs 15 in 221), so the power failure is partly self-inflicted. Correct action: report INSUFFICIENT_POWER, delete supports_h4, and if the comparison must appear use skill vs the in-group constant with a CI.

Re-derived from the raw cached xTB outputs: boltzmann_dipole reproduces for 39/39 molecules (max diff <0.005 D) and energy-range/weights are arithmetically correct (run_b100_conformers.py:201-208). Real defects: (a) 13/39 single_conformer_dipole values lie OUTSIDE the ensemble's own [dipole_min, dipole_max] (7 by >0.04 D: Dibutyl sebacate 4.842 vs [0.381,3.838], Dibutyl phthalate 3.977 vs [0.699,3.867], Tributylphosphate 3.924 vs [0.651,3.568], Nitroglycerin 3.552 vs [2.356,3.061]), so the 'single' geometry is not an ensemble member: the modelling table embeds with EmbedMolecule+MMFF (build_b100_xtb_coverage.py:118-126) and 221/257 dipoles are inherited from the earlier expansion run (:403-425), whereas the ensemble is ETKDGv3 multi-embed (run_b100_conformers.py:132-135). Part of the 'single vs Boltzmann' gap is therefore a pipeline difference, not conformer sampling; 4 of the 13 outside-range molecules are still flagged SINGLE_CONFORMER_RELIABLE, which is internally inconsistent. (b) The headline 30/36 is threshold-dependent: with tol 0.10/0.20/0.30/0.50 the unreliable count is 30/23/21/10, and neither tol=0.10 (:290) nor POLAR_FLOOR_D=0.30 (:302) is justified or sensitivity-tested in the script; 0.30 D is usable for the 3 n-alkanes it removes (all <0.07 D) but it is applied to the result itself (Boltzmann mean and single) so it classifies molecules out of the denominator using the outcome. (c) Only 6 conformers per molecule (median max Boltzmann weight 0.509 vs 0.167 uniform) with no Gibbs/entropy correction, on energy spans of 0.044-0.268 eV that are 1-6x the ~0.04 eV GFN2 error bar: the ensemble is not a converged thermodynamic average and the spreads are lower bounds. (d) Latent bugs: boltzmann_gap (:329-330) applies unfiltered weights to a filtered gap list, and round(x,4) if x else '' (:323-328) converts a genuine 0.0 into an empty cell - neither is triggered in this dataset. The qualitative finding (median relative spread 0.3227, median single-vs-Boltzmann deviation 0.0786) survives; the exact '30/36' does not.
